Cause captured with a traceback (a scratch copy of c05d19c with run.py's except block recording format_exc(), out/conf-fu/dbg/loopc-3.txt): story REFUSED: ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'alpha' at aisef2/runtime/process_range.py:95 _ps_table <- process_table <- ProcessRange.escaped <- probe/python_callable_v2.observe -> run.release(). _ps_table parses the output of `ps` with str.splitlines(), which also splits on U+2028/U+0085/U+000B/U+000C/U+001C-1E: any process on the macOS host whose command line holds one raw followed by text (another agent's test here) makes process_table() raise. Reproduced on demand with one process of mine (python3 -c with U+2028 in its source, alive 6 s): process_table raised ValueError ... 'alpha'. Linux (/proc) is not affected. Confinement is not involved (these tests' settings carry none).

found_outside_the_scope: aisef2/runtime/process_range.py::_ps_table (non-Linux): `r.stdout.splitlines()` splits a ps row at U+2028, U+0085, U+000B, U+000C, U+001C-1E when a command line holds one raw (macOS ps escapes \n as \012 but prints these as UTF-8), and `int(f[0])` of the continuation raises ValueError: aisef run on macOS refuses a story ('REFUSED: ValueError') while any such process exists; confine._survivors calls process_table too (Linux only: not reachable on macOS, where measure raises Unavailable first). Fix would be `.split('\n')` (and tolerating a row that does not parse). Not changed here: outside this WP; no test of it exists.
not_established: A host mount made after the reading before the session and before bubblewrap bound its parent in read-write, still mounted at the second reading, is no longer told from the sandbox's own (the union refused it). Bounded by: confine.wrap binds read-write only the workspace; a mount the host makes while the session runs reaches it only by propagation, which carries a host peer-group tag the policy already calls 'not shown to be the sandbox's own'. Argued from the code and the shared-tree record; NOT measured (no run mounts on the host in that window); bubblewrap's remount of submounts under --ro-bind not re-measured.

Unchanged and still fail-closed: a super block the reading before holds that the host unmounts before bubblewrap makes the session's own mounts frees its number for them -> a spurious refusal; window = reading before -> session mount setup. Not removed (cannot be told from a leak without the data to decide it).

The unrelated host activity of the real-guest reproduction is the driver's mounts in the controller's own mount namespace (a user+mount namespace of the container), not a second container or a CI host; the freed-number reuse itself is the kernel's.
